newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU states face telecoms deadlines on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: EU states face telecoms deadlines on Tuesday.

text.p: European Union countries on Tuesday face several key deadlines in the EU's plan for opening telecommunications markets to full competition by January 1, 1998.
By July 1, they are supposed to publish procedures for awarding licences for voice telephone services and public networks in an era without state phone monopolies.
The former monopolies must also publish the terms and conditions for "interconnection" deals allowing rivals to hook up to their networks and gain access to their customers.
Finally, EU states must ensure that enough phone numbers are available to handle the growing demand for telecoms services.
The measures aim to ensure that new players in the telecoms sector face a level playing field. But, as with other parts of the EU's plan, implementation varies from country to country.
To begin with, Greece, Ireland, Portugal and Spain have been authorised by the European Commission to delay implementation of some measures because they have "less developed" networks.

A Commission report published in May showed that phone companies in Britain, Denmark, Germany, France, Finland, Spain and Sweden had already published interconnection conditions. All of those countries but Spain had also submitted draft licensing conditions to the Commission, it said.

Britain, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden had also made available a sufficient number of fixed-line phone numbers and all of those but the Dutch also had enough mobile phone numbers.
However, events are moving quickly. Belgium, for example, adopted a package of telecoms legislation, including rules on interconnections, days after the Commission issued its report.
Former Belgian state monopoly Belgacom then announced last week it would publish on July 1 initial proposals for an interconnection system covering public telecoms networks.
It said it would develop more detailed proposals covering other market players sometime before December 31.

A Commission official said he was optimistic about the state of play on the eve of the July 1 deadline, noting that liberalisation was proceeding on or ahead of schedule in some of the EU's most important markets including France and Germany and pioneers Britain, Finland and Sweden.
A telecoms analyst said, however, that wide differences between countries were worrying for the EU's effort to create a single market.

Graham Finnie of Yankee Group Europe told a seminar in Brussels last week that while Britain and Sweden earned top marks for compliance with the EU's plan in a Yankee Group study, Greece scored only 2.2, Austria 2.6 and Portugal 2.9 out of a possible 5. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
